# The Re-Enchantment of the World

> A study companion to Bernard Stiegler and Ars Industrialis, The Re-Enchantment of the World (2006; English 2014): layered summaries, concepts and evaluated sources.

A fair-use study companion to Bernard Stiegler and Ars Industrialis, *Réenchanter le monde.
La valeur esprit contre le populisme industriel* (Flammarion, 2006), translated by Trevor
Arthur as *The Re-Enchantment of the World: The Value of Spirit against Industrial
Populism* (Bloomsbury, 2014). It gives the thesis, a one-page overview, a summary of each
part from abstract down to section level with page numbers, concept pages, a glossary, the
book's reception, and evaluated third-party sources. It paraphrases and quotes briefly; it
does not reproduce the book. Each link below is the Markdown version of a page of
https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/.

## Start here

- [Home](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/pr-preview/pr-4/index.md>): A study companion to Bernard Stiegler and Ars Industrialis, The Re-Enchantment of the World (2006; English 2014): layered summaries, concepts and evaluated sources.
- [Overview](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/pr-preview/pr-4/overview/index.md>): The book's argument arc in six steps, its place in Stiegler's work, and the Ars Industrialis project.

## The book

- [The parts of the book](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/pr-preview/pr-4/chapters/index.md>): The seven parts of The Re-Enchantment of the World, each summarized from abstract down to section level.
- [Translator's Preface](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/pr-preview/pr-4/chapters/00-translators-preface/index.md>): Trevor Arthur's Translator's Preface (pp. vii–ix): why savoir-faire and savoir-vivre stay in French, and why "spirit" falls short of esprit.
- [Introduction: What Is to Be Done?](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/pr-preview/pr-4/chapters/01-introduction-what-is-to-be-done/index.md>): Summary of the Introduction, "What Is to Be Done?" (pp. 1–10): Medef's "re-enchantment" slogan taken at its word, and the founding of Ars Industrialis.
- [2005 Manifesto](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/pr-preview/pr-4/chapters/02-manifesto-2005/index.md>): Summary of the 2005 Ars Industrialis manifesto (pp. 11–16): an industrial politics of spirit against the capture of attention.
- [2010 Manifesto](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/pr-preview/pr-4/chapters/03-manifesto-2010/index.md>): Summary of the 2010 Ars Industrialis manifesto (pp. 17–28), printed only in the English edition: pharmacology, care and the economy of contribution.
- [Ch. 1, The Re-Foundation of Society](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/pr-preview/pr-4/chapters/04-ch1-re-foundation-of-society/index.md>): Summary of Chapter 1, "The Re-Foundation of Society" (pp. 29–60), section by section, with a gloss of its notes.
- [Ch. 2, Against the Reign of Ignorance](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/pr-preview/pr-4/chapters/05-ch2-against-the-reign-of-ignorance/index.md>): Summary of Chapter 2, "Against the Reign of Ignorance" (pp. 61–93): knowledge against information, and investing in the value of spirit.
- [The Tunis Motion](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/pr-preview/pr-4/chapters/06-tunis-motion/index.md>): Summary of the Ars Industrialis motion addressed to the 2005 World Summit on the Information Society in Tunis (pp. 95–100).

## Concepts

- [Concepts](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/pr-preview/pr-4/concepts/index.md>): The nineteen concepts the book relies on, each with its definition, where it appears and how commentators read it.
- [Glossary](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/pr-preview/pr-4/GLOSSARY/index.md>): Short definitions of the book's terms, each linked to a full concept page.
- [Associated milieu / dissociated milieu](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/pr-preview/pr-4/concepts/associated-milieu/index.md>): Simondon's associated milieu, and Stiegler's contrast between associated and dissociated milieus of symbols and knowledge.
- [Care](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/pr-preview/pr-4/concepts/care/index.md>): Care (soin, epimeleia) as the practices and institutions that keep a technical pharmakon from turning toxic.
- [Disenchantment / re-enchantment](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/pr-preview/pr-4/concepts/disenchantment/index.md>): Weber's disenchantment of the world, and what the book means by re-enchanting it.
- [Economy of contribution](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/pr-preview/pr-4/concepts/economy-of-contribution/index.md>): The economy of contribution, the model Ars Industrialis proposes to replace consumerism.
- [Grammatization](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/pr-preview/pr-4/concepts/grammatization/index.md>): Grammatization: the discretization of speech, gesture and perception into reproducible marks, from the alphabet to digital code.
- [Hyperindustrial society](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/pr-preview/pr-4/concepts/hyperindustrial-society/index.md>): Hyperindustrial society: industrialization extended to services, culture, attention and knowledge.
- [Hypomnemata](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/pr-preview/pr-4/concepts/hypomnemata/index.md>): Hypomnemata: memory aids outside the mind, from Plato's critique of writing to Foucault and digital media.
- [Industrial populism](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/pr-preview/pr-4/concepts/industrial-populism/index.md>): Industrial populism: the populism produced by marketing and the program industries rather than by political movements.
- [Knowledge vs information](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/pr-preview/pr-4/concepts/knowledge-vs-information/index.md>): Knowledge against information: why Chapter 2 calls information entropic and knowledge negentropic.
- [Libidinal economy](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/pr-preview/pr-4/concepts/libidinal-economy/index.md>): The libidinal economy: how consumer capitalism channels desire, and how it exhausts desire into drives.
- [Otium / negotium](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/pr-preview/pr-4/concepts/otium-negotium/index.md>): Otium and negotium: studious leisure against business, and their link to subsistence, existence and consistence.
- [Pharmakon / pharmacology](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/pr-preview/pr-4/concepts/pharmakon/index.md>): Pharmakon and pharmacology: every technics as both remedy and poison.
- [Proletarianization](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/pr-preview/pr-4/concepts/proletarianization/index.md>): Proletarianization as the loss of knowledge by producers, consumers and knowledge workers.
- [Short-termism](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/pr-preview/pr-4/concepts/short-termism/index.md>): Short-termism as the temporal form of drive-based behaviour in finance, media and politics.
- [Spirit](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/pr-preview/pr-4/concepts/spirit/index.md>): Spirit (esprit) and Valéry's "value of spirit", the book's measure of what consumer capitalism lowers.
- [Symbolic misery](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/pr-preview/pr-4/concepts/symbolic-misery/index.md>): Symbolic misery: the loss of individuation that follows from losing a part in producing symbols.
- [Technologies of spirit](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/pr-preview/pr-4/concepts/technologies-of-spirit/index.md>): Technologies of spirit, and the contrast between psychotechnologies and nootechnologies.
- [Tertiary retention](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/pr-preview/pr-4/concepts/tertiary-retention/index.md>): Tertiary retention: memory held outside the living being in artefacts, after Husserl's primary and secondary retention.
- [Individuation, transindividuation, disindividuation](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/pr-preview/pr-4/concepts/transindividuation/index.md>): Individuation, transindividuation and disindividuation, after Simondon.

## Reference

- [Structure of the book](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/pr-preview/pr-4/STRUCTURE/index.md>): The contents of the English edition with page numbers, the differences from the French edition, and where each part comes from.
- [Index](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/pr-preview/pr-4/INDEX/index.md>): Cross-reference tables linking the book's parts, its concepts, the sources and the pages where each concept appears.
- [Reception and critique](<https://lmmx.github.io/stiegler-reenchantment-of-the-world/pr-preview/pr-4/reception/index.md>): How the book was received: reviews, lines of critique, errors in circulation, and Stiegler's own later revision.
